outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a production station for producing one or more layered beds made of magnetocaloric material, in particular particulate magnetocaloric material. Such a production station is designed to enable the controlled formation of layers of magnetocaloric particles, which may subsequently be used in a magnetocaloric heat exchanger or a similar thermal device.

The production station comprises a framework that supports the functional components of the station and provides the necessary structural stability during the production process. Arranged on or within the framework are a material receptacle, a dosing plate, and at least one reservoir. These components cooperate to receive, meter, and transfer particulate magnetocaloric material in a controlled manner.

The dosing plate is provided with at least one intake opening. This intake opening is configured to receive a defined quantity of particulate magnetocaloric material corresponding to one layer of the layered bed to be produced. By defining the geometry and volume of the intake opening, the dosing plate enables precise dosing of the material required for an individual layer.

At least one reservoir is arranged below the intake opening of the dosing plate. The reservoir is adapted to receive the particulate magnetocaloric material delivered through the dosing plate. In particular, the reservoir may be configured to receive one layer or a plurality of layers of the particulate magnetocaloric material, thereby forming a layered bed in a controlled and reproducible manner.

A shutter plate is arranged between the reservoir and the dosing plate. The shutter plate serves to control the filling of the reservoir with the particulate magnetocaloric material. To this end, the shutter plate is movable relative to the dosing plate and can be switched into a filling mode. In the filling mode, the relative movement between the shutter plate and the dosing plate allows material received in the intake opening of the dosing plate to pass into the reservoir. In another position, the shutter plate may block or restrict the passage of material, thereby preventing uncontrolled discharge and ensuring accurate layer formation.

Through the coordinated interaction of the framework, material receptacle, dosing plate, reservoir, and shutter plate, the production station enables reliable and precise production of one or more layered beds of magnetocaloric material. This arrangement is particularly suitable for handling particulate material and for forming layers with reproducible thickness, composition, and distribution.
outputs.L4:
A production station is provided for manufacturing one or more layered beds made from particulate magnetocaloric material. The station includes a supporting framework on which the principal functional components are mounted and aligned with one another. These components include a material receptacle for receiving or holding particulate magnetocaloric material, a dosing plate arranged to meter the material in a controlled manner, a reservoir positioned to receive the dosed material, and a movable shutter plate that selectively opens and closes the flow path between the material receptacle and the reservoir.

During operation, particulate magnetocaloric material is supplied to the material receptacle. The dosing plate defines the quantity, distribution, or pattern of material that is to be transferred for forming a layer of the bed. By moving the shutter plate between different positions, the production station can either permit material to pass through the dosing plate into the reservoir or prevent further filling. In this way, the shutter plate acts as a controllable gate, allowing the reservoir to be filled only when required and only to the desired extent.

The controlled interaction between the dosing plate and the shutter plate enables accurate metering of the particulate material. This is particularly useful when producing layered beds in which each layer must have a defined thickness, mass, composition, particle size, or spatial distribution. Different magnetocaloric materials, or different fractions of the same material, may be introduced successively to form a multilayer structure with tailored thermal and magnetic properties.

Once the reservoir has received the required amount of material, the material can be delivered to a bed-forming region or mold to create a layer. The process may then be repeated to build up one or more layered beds. Each layer can be formed under controlled conditions, improving reproducibility and reducing variations in the final product. The arrangement also helps limit material waste and supports automated or semi-automated production.

By using a framework-mounted receptacle, dosing plate, reservoir, and movable shutter plate, the production station provides a reliable and precise mechanism for producing layered beds of particulate magnetocaloric material. The selective control of filling through the dosing plate allows the station to form layers efficiently and consistently, thereby supporting the manufacture of magnetocaloric beds suitable for use in magnetic refrigeration, heat pumping, or other thermal management applications.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, but it is also one of the most important. It is called the definite article, and its job is to point to something specific. When we say “the book,” we are not talking about just any book; we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener can identify.

This simple word helps make communication clearer. For example, “a car” could mean any car, but “the car” refers to a certain car. Because of this, “the” gives language precision and direction. It helps people understand whether we are speaking generally or referring to something known.

“The” is also used with unique things, such as “the sun,” “the moon,” and “the sky.” Since there is usually only one of these in everyday conversation, the word makes sense naturally. It can also appear before names of rivers, oceans, famous buildings, and groups, such as “the Nile,” “the Pacific Ocean,” and “the United Nations.”

Although “the” may seem ordinary, it plays a powerful role in English. Without it, sentences would often sound incomplete or unclear. This tiny word shows how even the simplest parts of language can carry great meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract/claim describing a production station for manufacturing layered beds of particulate magnetocaloric material, including a framework, material receptacle, dosing plate, reservoir, and movable shutter plate for controlled filling.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A production station for manufacturing layered beds of particulate magnetocaloric material is disclosed. The production station comprises a supporting framework configured to receive and position a material receptacle having at least one cavity for forming a bed layer. A dosing plate is arranged relative to the receptacle and includes one or more dosing openings defining a predetermined volume of particulate magnetocaloric material to be delivered. A reservoir is mounted above or adjacent the dosing plate and is configured to supply particulate magnetocaloric material to the dosing openings. A movable shutter plate is arranged between the reservoir and the material receptacle, or relative to the dosing plate, and is selectively displaceable between a closed position, in which discharge of particulate material from the dosing openings is prevented, and an open position, in which the particulate material is released into the receptacle. Movement of the shutter plate thereby enables controlled filling of the receptacle with metered quantities of particulate magnetocaloric material to form one or more uniform layers of a layered magnetocaloric bed.

**Claim**

1. A production station for manufacturing a layered bed of particulate magnetocaloric material, the production station comprising:  
   a framework configured to support and position components of the production station;  
   a material receptacle supported by the framework and having at least one receiving cavity configured to receive particulate magnetocaloric material for formation of a layer of the layered bed;  
   a dosing plate arranged in alignment with the material receptacle, the dosing plate comprising at least one dosing aperture configured to define a predetermined quantity of particulate magnetocaloric material;  
   a reservoir configured to contain and supply particulate magnetocaloric material to the dosing plate; and  
   a movable shutter plate arranged to selectively control passage of particulate magnetocaloric material from the dosing plate to the material receptacle,  
   wherein the movable shutter plate is displaceable between a blocking position, in which the particulate magnetocaloric material is retained in or above the at least one dosing aperture, and a filling position, in which the particulate magnetocaloric material is permitted to pass into the at least one receiving cavity of the material receptacle, thereby enabling controlled filling of the material receptacle with a metered amount of particulate magnetocaloric material for producing a layer of the layered bed.

2. The production station of claim 1, wherein the movable shutter plate is slidable relative to the dosing plate to selectively align or misalign shutter openings with the at least one dosing aperture.

3. The production station of claim 1, wherein the material receptacle comprises a plurality of receiving cavities configured to form a plurality of corresponding bed regions.

4. The production station of claim 1, wherein the dosing plate comprises a plurality of dosing apertures having volumes selected according to a desired thickness or mass of a layer of the particulate magnetocaloric material.

5. The production station of claim 1, wherein the reservoir is configured to hold particulate magnetocaloric material of a selected composition, particle size, Curie temperature, or magnetocaloric grade.

6. The production station of claim 1, further comprising an actuator coupled to the movable shutter plate and configured to move the shutter plate between the blocking position and the filling position.

7. The production station of claim 1, wherein the framework is configured to permit sequential filling of the material receptacle with different particulate magnetocaloric materials to produce a layered bed having layers of different magnetocaloric properties.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical invention description in patent language for a station that doses particulate magnetocaloric material into layered beds using a receptacle, dosing plate, reservoir, and controllable shutter mechanism.
counterfactuals.output:
## Technical Invention Description

The invention relates to a station for producing a layered bed comprising particulate magnetocaloric material, in particular for manufacturing active magnetic regenerator beds or heat-exchange bodies used in magnetocaloric thermal machines. The station is configured to dose, meter, and deposit discrete quantities of particulate magnetocaloric material in a controlled manner so as to form one or more layers within a receptacle.

In one embodiment, the station comprises a receptacle configured to receive and support the particulate magnetocaloric material during deposition. The receptacle may define a cavity, channel, compartment, cartridge, regenerator housing, tray, or mold into which the particulate material is introduced. The receptacle may be stationary or may be movable relative to a dosing assembly, for example by a linear actuator, indexing table, conveyor, rotary carrier, or robotic positioning system. The receptacle may further comprise side walls, partitions, spacers, screens, porous retainers, or flow-distribution structures adapted to define the geometry of the layered bed.

The station further comprises a reservoir adapted to contain a supply of particulate magnetocaloric material. The particulate magnetocaloric material may comprise granules, beads, chips, flakes, pellets, crushed particles, spherical particles, sieved fractions, or other particulate forms of magnetocaloric compounds, alloys, composites, or intermetallic materials. In particular embodiments, different reservoirs may contain different magnetocaloric materials, different Curie-temperature grades, different particle-size fractions, or different compositions intended to be arranged in a predetermined layered order.

A dosing plate is arranged between the reservoir and the receptacle. The dosing plate comprises at least one dosing aperture, recess, pocket, cavity, channel, through-hole, or metering volume configured to receive a predetermined volume of particulate magnetocaloric material from the reservoir. The metering volume may be selected according to a desired layer mass, layer thickness, packing density, or bed geometry. In certain embodiments, the dosing plate comprises a plurality of dosing apertures distributed over an area corresponding to a desired deposition pattern in the receptacle. The plurality of apertures may have equal or different volumes, cross-sections, depths, or spacings to provide a uniform or spatially varied particulate distribution.

The station further comprises a controllable shutter mechanism configured to selectively permit and prevent transfer of particulate magnetocaloric material from the dosing plate into the receptacle. The shutter mechanism may be arranged beneath the dosing plate and may be movable between a closed position, in which material held in the dosing aperture or apertures is retained, and an open position, in which the retained material is released into the receptacle by gravity, vibration, pneumatic assistance, mechanical displacement, or a combination thereof. The shutter mechanism may include a sliding shutter plate, rotary shutter, gate, iris, segmented closure, valve plate, perforated plate, or other movable closure member. In one implementation, the shutter plate includes one or more openings selectively alignable with the dosing aperture or apertures of the dosing plate. When the shutter openings are misaligned with the dosing apertures, discharge is prevented. When the shutter openings are aligned, the metered material is discharged into the receptacle.

In use, particulate magnetocaloric material is supplied from the reservoir to the dosing plate. The material fills the dosing aperture or apertures of the dosing plate under the influence of gravity, vibration, agitation, fluidization, stirring, or mechanical sweeping. Excess particulate material may be removed from an upper surface of the dosing plate by a leveling member, doctor blade, wiper, scraper, vibratory screed, or reciprocating spreader such that the quantity retained in the dosing aperture or apertures corresponds substantially to a predetermined dose. The shutter mechanism remains in the closed position while the dosing aperture or apertures are filled and leveled.

After dosing, the receptacle is positioned beneath the dosing plate and the shutter mechanism is actuated to the open position. The particulate magnetocaloric material contained in the dosing aperture or apertures is thereby released into the receptacle to form a layer or partial layer. The shutter mechanism may then be returned to the closed position, and the process may be repeated to build up a bed composed of multiple layers. Between successive dosing operations, the receptacle and/or dosing plate may be displaced laterally, vertically, rotationally, or angularly to control placement, distribution, compaction, or layer thickness.

In a preferred embodiment, the station is configured to form a layered bed in which successive layers comprise magnetocaloric materials having different transition temperatures. A first reservoir may contain a first particulate magnetocaloric material having a first Curie temperature, while a second reservoir may contain a second particulate magnetocaloric material having a second Curie temperature. A controller may select one of the reservoirs, control filling of the corresponding dosing plate volume, actuate the shutter mechanism, and thereby deposit the selected material into the receptacle in a prescribed sequence. In this manner, a graded magnetocaloric bed may be produced with high repeatability.

The station may further comprise one or more sensors for monitoring dosing accuracy, material level, shutter position, receptacle position, layer height, deposited mass, vibration state, or environmental conditions. Suitable sensors include load cells, optical sensors, capacitive sensors, inductive sensors, laser distance sensors, cameras, encoders, pressure sensors, and magnetic or mechanical position sensors. A control unit may receive signals from the sensors and control operation of the reservoir feeder, dosing plate, leveling device, shutter actuator, and receptacle positioning mechanism.

The controllable shutter mechanism may be driven by an electric motor, solenoid, pneumatic cylinder, hydraulic actuator, piezoelectric actuator, cam mechanism, magnetic actuator, or shape-memory actuator. The actuator may be configured to provide rapid opening and closing in order to achieve clean release of the particulate material and to minimize smearing, partial discharge, bridging, or uncontrolled leakage. The shutter mechanism may include sealing surfaces, low-friction coatings, hardened wear surfaces, ceramic inserts, polymer liners, or anti-adhesion coatings to reduce contamination and abrasion caused by the magnetocaloric particles.

In certain embodiments, the station includes a vibration or tapping device coupled to the reservoir, dosing plate, shutter mechanism, or receptacle. The vibration device may promote filling of the dosing apertures, reduce particle bridging, improve discharge completeness, or compact the deposited layer. The vibration amplitude, frequency, and duration may be controlled according to particle size, particle shape, material density, or desired packing fraction. In further embodiments, a gas flow, vacuum assistance, electrostatic discharge device, ionizer, or humidity-control system may be provided to improve flowability and repeatability of dosing.

The dosing plate may be interchangeable, thereby permitting rapid adjustment of the dose volume or deposition pattern. A set of dosing plates may be provided, each having different aperture dimensions corresponding to different layer masses, layer thicknesses, or receptacle geometries. The dosing plate may be removably mounted in a frame by clamps, locating pins, quick-release fasteners, magnetic holders, or precision guides. The station may thereby accommodate different regenerator sizes and different magnetocaloric bed architectures without requiring substantial redesign.

The reservoir may be configured as a hopper, cartridge, bin, cassette, funnel, magazine, or sealed container. In one embodiment, the reservoir is removable and replaceable so that different magnetocaloric material grades can be loaded without cross-contamination. The reservoir may include an outlet opening positioned above the dosing plate, and a feed-control member may regulate the supply of particulate material to the dosing plate. The feed-control member may include a valve, auger, vibratory feeder, belt feeder, rotary feeder, slide gate, or reciprocating shoe.

To manufacture a layered magnetocaloric bed, the controller may execute a stored dosing recipe. The dosing recipe may define, for each layer, at least one of material type, dose volume, target mass, layer thickness, receptacle position, shutter opening duration, vibration profile, leveling operation, compaction operation, and inspection step. The controller may compare measured data with target values and may adjust subsequent dosing operations to compensate for deviations. For example, if a measured deposited mass is below a target value, the controller may increase vibration duration, repeat a partial dose, or select a dosing aperture with a larger volume.

The layered bed produced by the station may comprise layers having sharply defined interfaces or partially blended interfaces, depending on process parameters. Where sharply defined layers are desired, the station may employ low-drop-height deposition, controlled shutter opening, and minimal vibration after release. Where blended transition regions are desired, the station may introduce controlled vibration or sequential partial dosing of different materials.

The station provides accurate volumetric dosing of particulate magnetocaloric material while limiting material waste and reducing manual handling. The use of a dosing plate in combination with a controllable shutter mechanism enables repeatable formation of thin layers and permits automation of graded bed production. The station is particularly advantageous for magnetocaloric materials, which may be brittle, abrasive, expensive, composition-sensitive, or susceptible to oxidation or contamination. By metering discrete volumes prior to release, the station improves layer uniformity and enables reproducible thermal and magnetic performance of the resulting regenerator bed.

In further embodiments, the station may be enclosed within a controlled atmosphere chamber. The chamber may be filled with inert gas, dry air, nitrogen, argon, or another protective atmosphere to prevent oxidation, moisture uptake, or degradation of the magnetocaloric material. The chamber may include glove ports, purge connections, filters, pressure regulation, and particulate containment features.

The invention also contemplates a method of dosing particulate magnetocaloric material into a layered bed. The method comprises supplying particulate magnetocaloric material from a reservoir to a dosing plate, filling at least one metering aperture of the dosing plate with the particulate material, retaining the material in the metering aperture by a controllable shutter mechanism, positioning a receptacle beneath the dosing plate, actuating the shutter mechanism to release the retained material into the receptacle, and repeating the foregoing steps to form a plurality of layers. The method may further comprise selecting different magnetocaloric materials for different layers, leveling excess material from the dosing plate, vibrating the dosing plate or receptacle, measuring deposited mass or layer height, and controlling subsequent dosing operations based on feedback.

Accordingly, the disclosed station enables controlled and repeatable fabrication of layered particulate magnetocaloric beds using a receptacle, dosing plate, reservoir, and controllable shutter mechanism, and is suitable for automated production of graded active magnetic regenerators and related magnetocaloric heat-transfer structures.
